correctness.rationale: For three distinct ordered nodes, the degree-two exact moment system is uniquely solved by Lagrange formulas, yielding an exact sign event with 12 Gaussian label/sign assignments. Integration gives P(q). Writing q=exp(t) expresses P as a positive constant times convolution of the strictly log-concave density of log|N(0,1)| with F(1-F), itself strictly log-concave via strictly monotone Gaussian hazards; strict convolution log-concavity proves exactly one maximizer and endpoint tails vanish. Its derivative equation is exact. Published Theorem 2.4 of arXiv:1906.02096 independently justifies the flat limit even for Gaussian integration. Strong-shape positivity is proved pointwise via K_h->I. The embedded checker passed 30,122 separate finite assertions for moment constraints, event signs, Monte Carlo probability estimates, critical numbers, and high precision fixed-node flat limits. The program is not treated as a global proof.

originality.rationale: Available published-finding corpus semantic searches, accessible own current-week and past scientific claims, published sources and relevant primary full text reveal no implication of the exact Gaussian random-three-node all-positive probability or globally unique optimal proposal variance. The literature already proves the Bayesian quadrature construction, flat-kernel polynomial limit and other positivity models; these are credited as existing premises. Full-text comparisons distinguish matching terminology from exact event and parameters, and residual historical-priority risk remains.
residual_risks: Unindexed equivalent Gaussian random-node probability calculations or stronger log-concave probability results might predate this finding.
The reported decimal root and maximum are numerical quadrature approximations, not interval-certified endpoints.
Flat-kernel limits are pointwise for distinct nodes, and numerical ill conditioning can spoil floating point signs.
No independent external mathematical validation has been performed.

value.rationale: Three independently sampled nodes are the minimal nontrivial setting where a unique quadratic-exact interpolatory rule can have mixed-sign weights. The exact all-positive probability, unique optimal Gaussian proposal variance and its approximately 24.7% maximum are a natural, motivated positivity-reliability benchmark for Gaussian-kernel Bayesian quadrature; they quantify an actual proposal-design tradeoff and explain the sharp gap from matched-scale sampling. This is not a routine normalization or an arbitrary parameter slice; no claim of improved integration accuracy is made.
